Declare that a point layer draws a volcano plot

Source: R/ggplot2_volcano_declaration.R
maidr_volcano.Rd

maidr_volcano() is ggplot2::geom_point() with three things added: the author saying that the points are a volcano plot, the significance threshold the chart is read against, and two aesthetics for what each point is – label (the gene) and region (any grouping announced alongside it, such as up- or down-regulated). A declared layer is read as a volcano: the description says how many points clear the threshold and names them, a rotor mode steps through only those points, and every point is announced with its label and region. The same points drawn with geom_point() read as a scatter, which says two coordinates and withholds which gene they belong to.

Nothing about the picture changes: the geom draws exactly what geom_point() draws, and neither label nor region reaches a mark. Draw the threshold lines yourself, with geom_hline() and geom_vline(); maidr leaves reference lines out of the reading.

The volcano layer type [experimental] is one of the experimental plot types: it has not been through a user study, and its reading may change without a deprecation period. See "Experimental Plot Types" in the README.

Usage

maidr_volcano(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  significance,
  effect = NULL,
  direction = c("above", "below"),
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

Arguments

mapping

Aesthetics, as for ggplot2::geom_point(): x (the effect size, such as a log2 fold change) and y (the significance, such as -log10 of the p value) are required. label may name each point (the gene) and region the group it belongs to; both are announced with the point. Every other point aesthetic (colour, size, alpha, ...) behaves exactly as it does there.

data

The layer's data, as for ggplot2::geom_point().

position

Position adjustment, as for ggplot2::geom_point().

...

Other arguments passed to the layer, as for ggplot2::geom_point() – except stat, which is fixed at "identity": a declared layer is always drawn from the author's own points.

significance

The significance cutoff on the y axis, one number in the units y is announced in. Required.

effect

The effect-size cutoff, applied to the magnitude of x, or NULL (the default) for none.

direction

Which side of significance the significant points are on: "above" (the default) for a -log10(p) axis, "below" for a raw p value.

na.rm

If FALSE (the default), rows with missing values are removed with a warning.

show.legend

Whether this layer is included in the legends.

inherit.aes

If FALSE, the plot's default aesthetics are not inherited.

Value

A ggplot2 layer, to be added to a plot with +.

The threshold is stated, never guessed

A point is significant when its y is at or above significance (at or below it with direction = "below") and, when effect is given, the magnitude of its x is at least effect – a fold change of -2 is as large an effect as one of +2. Both are in the units the axes are announced in, which are the data's own: significance = -log10(0.05) for y = -log10(pvalue), and significance = 0.05, direction = "below" for a raw p value, even on a log-scaled y axis, whose points are announced as the p values they are.

There is no default, because these charts sit on transformed axes whose conventions differ by field and by tool, and a line drawn in the wrong place would put every point on the wrong side of it without saying so.

See also

maidr_manhattan() for a Manhattan plot; save_html() and show() for rendering the declared chart

Examples

if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  genes <- data.frame(
    gene = c("TP53", "MYC", "EGFR", "BRCA1", "KRAS", "PTEN", "GAPDH"),
    log2fc = c(2.8, -3.1, 1.6, -0.4, 0.3, -2.2, 0.1),
    padj = c(1e-8, 1e-6, 0.02, 0.4, 0.7, 1e-4, 0.9)
  )

  volcano <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    genes,
    ggplot2::aes(x = log2fc, y = -log10(padj))
  ) +
    maidr_volcano(
      ggplot2::aes(label = gene),
      significance = -log10(0.05),
      effect = 1
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed") +
    ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1, 1), linetype = "dashed") +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "log2 fold change", y = "-log10 adjusted p")

  if (interactive()) {
    show(volcano)
  }
}
